# Destroy a Stack

We recommend destroying a Stack in phases to ensure HCP Terraform destroys your infrastructure safely. Delete your Stack deployments before deleting the Stack itself to ensure you do not leave any unmanaged infrastructure behind.

##  Requirements

You must be a member of a team with one of the following permissions:

* [Organization-level **Manage all projects**](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/permissions/organization#manage-all-projects)
* [Project-level **Maintain**](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/permissions/project#project-maintain) or higher

### Stack recovery requirements

You can recover a Stack that has been deleted within 30 days from the date and time it was deleted. You must meet the following requirements to recover a Stack:
- [**Allow deleted workspaces and stacks to be recoverable**](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/organizations/settings#allow-deleted-workspaces-and-stacks-to-be-recoverable) must be enabled for your organization.  <!-- BEGIN: TFC:only name:pnp-callout -->
- You must have a paid subscription. Refer to the [pricing page](https://www.hashicorp.com/en/pricing?tab=terraform) for more information.<!-- END: TFC:only name:pnp-callout -->

## Delete Stack deployments

You can delete Stack deployments through the HCP Terraform UI or deployment configuration file.

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="UI">

1. Sign in to [HCP Terraform](https://app.terraform.io/) or Terraform Enterprise and navigate to the Stack you want to delete.
1. In the page header, click **New configuration**. The **Roll out a new configuration** modal appears.
1. Select **Tear down Stack** from the **Configuration type** dropdown.
1. Enter `teardown` in the confirmation input, then click **Start**.

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Deployment configuration file">

Add the `destroy` argument to every `deployment` block in your deployment configuration file. The following example destroys the `production` deployment using the `destroy` argument:

<CodeBlockConfig filename="deployments.tfdeploy.hcl" highlight="6">

```hcl
deployment "production" {
  inputs = {
    region          = "us-west-2"
    instances       = 2
  }
  destroy = true
}
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

After uploading the updated deployment configuration file and approving the subsequent plan, HCP Terraform destroys any infrastructure for the `production` deployment.

</Tab>

</Tabs>

After deleting all Stack deployments, you can safely delete the Stack.

## Delete a Stack

Before deleting a Stack in HCP Terraform, we strongly recommend [deleting all of that Stack’s deployments](#delete-stack-deployments). Once your Stack contains no deployments, you can delete a Stack by performing the following steps:

1. Sign in to [HCP Terraform](https://app.terraform.io/) or Terraform Enterprise and navigate to the Stack you want to delete.
1. Select **Settings** in the navigation menu.
1. Select **Destruction and Deletion**.
1. Click **Delete stack <STACK_NAME>**.
1. Enter `delete` in the confirmation modal, then click **Delete Stack**.

By following the steps above, you can forcefully delete a Stack without removing its deployments first. However, your Stack’s deletion does not affect its resources, so they continue without management, and you have to clean them up manually.

## Recover a Stack

You have 30 days to recover a discarded Stack. During the recovery window, HCP Terraform continue to record new configuration versions committed through VCS webhooks, but commits don’t trigger new runs. You can’t recover a Stack that has the same name as an existing Stack.

Complete the following steps to recover a discarded workspace:

1. Sign in to [HCP Terraform](https://app.terraform.io/) or Terraform Enterprise and navigate to the organization that contained the Stack.
1. Click **Settings** in the sidebar, then click **Recoverable items**.
1. For the Stack you want to recover, click the **Actions** dropdown and choose **Recover**.
1. When prompted, click **Recover**. HCP Terraform recovers the Stack to its last known state before deletion.
